## Summary  
The 2025 cotton crop in Monroe County is finished. The county‑level yield estimate is **843 lb/acre** with an 80 % range of 633 to 1046 lb/acre. The field showed a small low‑NDVI zone in the east.

## Crop health  
Peak NDVI was 0.84 on 2025‑08‑14. Peak NDRE was 0.55. Clear satellite images were available for 59 days. Most of the field had NDVI above 0.84. The low zone had NDVI 0.715. The high zone had NDVI 0.872.

## Problem areas  
A low‑NDVI zone covers 2.8 % (2.7 ac) in the east. Soil pH values of 5.8, 5.3 and 5.0 are below the optimal 6.0 to 6.5 range. The water balance is –7.0 in, giving a large deficit. No poorly drained soils were found.

## Weather  
Total rain was 27.9 in. Water balance was –7.0 in. Heat stress days were 20. The longest dry spell was 24 days. Deficit severity is large. Summer heat reached 95.0 °F.

## Soil  
The field is 47.3 % Lucedale fine sandy loam, 31.7 % Malbis loam, 13.4 % Bama fine sandy loam and 7.5 % Lucedale loam. All soils are well or moderately well drained. Available water ranges from 5.7 in to 6.4 in. Soil pH is 5.8, 5.3 or 5.0.

## Yield outlook  
Summer heat averaged 95.0 °F versus a typical 90.8 °F, which lowered the estimate. August water balance was –2.7 in versus a typical –1.7 in, which lowered the estimate. Summer rainfall was 12.6 in versus a typical 14.6 in, which raised the estimate. Longest dry spell was 25.0 days versus a typical 22.8 days, which raised the estimate.

## What to check next  
- Apply lime to raise soil pH toward 6.0‑6.5.  
- Plan supplemental irrigation to reduce large water deficit.  
- Review planting window and ensure soil temperature reaches at least 65 °F before planting.  
- Monitor summer heat forecasts and adjust management to avoid heat stress.
